title: Write a date and time
hook: Would you leave the vaccination plan vague or put it on the calendar?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Distinguish intention strength from an implementation plan with a concrete time.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Distinguish intention strength from an implementation plan with a concrete time.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: A toy appointment is planned at 08:00, but the available window is 09:00–12:00. How far is it outside that window? Toy inputs A=[8, 9, 12]; B=[10, 9, 12].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[1, 8, 3], [0, 10, 3]]. Labels: Conflict hours, Planned hour, Window hours.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: Writing a specific time exposes a concrete feasibility constraint that a general intention can leave hidden. The comparison chooses a time inside the window. A feasible plan is not a guarantee that the appointment will be completed.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Planned hour=10, Available from=9, Available until=12. What is Conflict hours? Answer: 0.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Planned hour=10, Available from=9, Available until=12. What is Conflict hours?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 0. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: Prompting employees to write down the date and time they'd get a flu shot raised vaccination 4.2 percentage points (Milkman, Beshears, Choi, Laibson & Madrian, 2011).
sourceProvenance.pointer: 500-behavioral-economics-findings.md entry 342: Milkman, Beshears, Choi, Laibson & Madrian, 2011
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Distinguish intention strength from an implementation plan with a concrete time.
